{{Recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Beverages|Beverages]] | [[Cookbook:Raw Diet|Raw Diet]]

'''Almond milk''' is a [[Cookbook:Nondairy Milk|plant milk]] used in a variety of cultures. Plant milks are often a [[Cookbook:Vegan Substitutions#Dairy|vegan substitute for dairy]], and are suitable for people with lactose intolerance or who want a dairy milk alternative.

Unlike cow’s milk, almond milk contains no cholesterol, is much lower in saturated fat, and lacks casein. It is therefore suitable for those with casein allergies.<ref>{{Cite journal
| author      = G. H. Docena
| author2     = R. Fernandez
| author3     = F. G.  Chirdo
| author4     = C. A.  Fossati
| editor      = Thomas Bieber
| date        = June 1996
| accessdate  = 2007-04-29
| title       = Identification of casein as the major allergenic and antigenic protein of cow's milk
| journal     = Allergy
| volume      = 51
| issue       = 6
| pages       = 412-416
| publisher   = John Wiley & Sons
| location    = Hoboken, NJ
| issn        = 0105-4538
| doi         = 10.1111/j.1398-9995.1996.tb04639.x 
| oclc        = 119867765
| PMID        = 883766
| url         = http://www3.interscience.wiley.com/journal/119209344/abstract
}}</ref> Unlike [[Cookbook:Soy Milk|soy milk]], this recipe is suitable for those who wish to avoid soy for various reasons.

== Ingredients ==
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (236 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Almond|almonds]]
*{{cups|3}} pure [[Cookbook:Water|water]], such as {{cb|rosewater}}, orange blossom water, spring water, distilled water, or iodized water
*3 [[Cookbook:Date|dates]]

== Equipment ==
*[[Cookbook:Measuring Cup|Measuring cup]]
*Bowl
*[[Cookbook:Blender|Blender]]
*[[Cookbook:Sieve|Sieve]] or sprout/nut-milk bag
*[[Cookbook:Wooden Spoon|Wooden spoon]] 
*Pitcher

== Procedure ==
#Put the almonds into a bowl, and cover them with at least one 1 [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] (2.5 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]]) of water. Leave them in the refrigerator overnight, and then drain the water. This is called sprouting or steeping.
#Put the drained almonds into a [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]], and blend in the 3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (708 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) of water. The mixture will start clear and quickly change color. Stop blending after a few minutes when there is no visible change in color or consistency anymore.
#Strain this mixture over a pitcher. You can either strain it through a fine sieve by squeezing the milk from the moist mixture through the sieve with a wooden spoon, or simply place mesh sometimes called a sprout or nut-milk bag that is usually made of nylon on top of the pitcher in order to squeeze the mixture through the mesh by hand. You may either discard the pulp or use it for other recipes, such as mixing it into almond {{cb|agar jelly}}.
#Return the strained almond milk into the blender. Add the dates and blend until there is no longer any visible change in color or consistency.
#Refrigerate or pour into a drinking cup and consume.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* If you would like to substitute a different sweetener for the dates, try natural sweeteners, such or stevia or [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]] instead of [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] or syrup, if you can. Just bear in mind that using honey would make this recipe not vegan.

== Warnings ==
*Do not use bitter almonds, since the combination of bitter almonds and water releases cyanide.<ref>
{{Cite web
|url=http://www.revolutionhealth.com/healthy-living/vitamin-index/bitter-almond-ns
|url-status=deviated
|archivedate=8 Jul 2009
|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090708020914/http://www.revolutionhealth.com/healthy-living/vitamin-index/bitter-almond-ns
|title=Bitter Almond
|date=March 8, 2007 
|accessdate=2009-05-14
|work=revolutionhealth
}}</ref>
*Do not keep the mixture from step 2 above for more than two days, since it spoils quickly. It's best to make it fresh.
*There are recipes that use a stove or boiling water, but heat destroys the food enzymes in the almonds.
*Using water that is not pure, such as tap water, may have an adverse taste.
